key_insight: Automatic differentiation reveals that aerodynamic information is transported non-uniformly in compressible flow, creating localized high-observability regions for sparse pressure sensing.
engineering_relevance: This provides a quantitative way to choose informative sensor locations for inverse aerodynamics, improving parameter recovery from limited measurements.
method: Differentiable shock-capturing immersed-boundary solver for unsteady compressible flow
Backpropagate through the full flow solution to compute an observability metric from pressure sensitivities
Use inverse-learning experiments to compare observability with parameter learnability
evidence_signal: The abstract reports observability maps and inverse-learning tests across different flow regimes and airfoil geometries, showing that sensor effectiveness and convergence vary with both conditions.
watch_item: High observability does not always mean best parameter-inference performance, so sensor choice may need validation against the specific inverse problem.
paper_title: Information Transport and Observability in Compressible Aerodynamics
